Why Richardson businesses miss calls

Richardson’s Telecom Corridor has long made it a technology center for North Texas, and the University of Texas at Dallas adds students, researchers and young professionals. Many customers here work in tech and expect a fast, clear response. Older neighborhoods also need steady plumbing, roofing and repair work. That gives local firms two very different callers, and both will quickly try another company if nobody answers.

Which Richardson businesses benefit most?

  • Accountants and CPAs: Tech workers and small firms can book meetings fast.
  • Dental offices: Patients can book during a work break.
  • HVAC and contractors: Older homes bring constant repair calls.

Here is an example of how a call might go. Your script, rules and wording would be set up with you.

Caller: I work until six. Can someone call me back after that?

AI receptionist: Notes the request, books an evening callback and sends your team a summary.

Can you keep your Richardson phone number?

Yes. Richardson callers will usually see the 214, 469, 972 and 945 area codes, and you can keep the number customers already know. Forward it to the AI for all calls, only after hours, or only when your team does not pick up. We can also set up a new local number. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
